About this item

  • NOTES: Aqara Hub is required and sold separately. Requires a secured 2. 4 gigahertz WiFi network connection. One Aqara Hub can connect up to 32 Aqara devices.
  • FLOOD DETECTION: Whenever the Aqara Water Leak Sensor detects water, it can send an alert to your phone and activate the local alarm on the Aqara Hub to prevent leaks and flooding.
  • HOME AUTOMATION: Controls and triggers Aqara connected devices when excess water is detected.
  • WIRELESS & SENSITIVE: No wiring or screws are required. The ultra mini design allows you to put it anywhere that dripping and leaking could happen. Our water leak sensor is designed with sensitive leak probes which the threshold of the water level is 0.5mm.
  • INDUSTRY-LEADING QUALITY: Durable IP67 water-proof housing with rust-proof exterior coating. Zigbee2MQTT and comparable third-party USB dongles are not officially supported by Aqara. Full product functionality may be limited or unavailable.

Product Description

Smart Control in Apple Home App

Works with other HomeKit-enabled accessories in Apple Home app to make your life easier.

IP67 Waterproof Rating

Aqara Water Leak Sensor meets IP67 dustproof and waterproof rating. It can work in humid and dusty environments.

Note: Aqara Hub is required to enable this product to work.

Triggers Alarm When Flooding is Detected

When the water level reaches up to 0.5mm, the Water Leak Sensor will trigger the Hub to sound an alarm and send a notification to your phone.

Advanced Technology

The outer shell is made out of anti-UV material and protects the sensor from discoloration.

The sensor is also energy efficient and one battery can last over 2 years under normal usage.

Amazon Customer
5 out of 5 stars
Reassuring water leak detector
I got a couple of these to go under sinks after a recent water leak. They're nice and small and will sit discreetly at the back of a cupboard. The information suggests pairing with an aqara hub, but as they're zigbee devices, they also pair with my sonoff zigbee dongle plus. Using ZHA they expose moisture (wet or dry), device temp (as expected, this runs hotter than ambient temperature) , firmware and battery. The battery showed 84% immediately, then rapidly 73% - this is something I've noticed with some of my other aqara zigbee devices, although the battery then seems to stay very stable at that level for a long time. The first time I tried to pair the device was unsuccessful. A 5 second press of the reset button didn't seem to make if visible to my zigbee network. The second time, I bought it close to my zigbee dongle, and held the reset button until the blue light flashed, and continued to hold the button until it paired with ZHA - this took approximately 20 seconds. In a crude test I poured about 10 ml of water next to the device and let it trickly underneath - it took about a minute, but then triggered my leak detection automation. I think it took some time for the water to spread and get in contact with the 2 sensors which are underneath the device. When I remove it from the water, it immediately records dry. When I placed it back in the small 10ml pool of water on the surface, it immediately recorded wet again. I'm pretty happy that this will rapidly detect a fairly small leak.

    In the realm of home automation and smart living, the Aqara Water Leak Sensor stands as a beacon of reliability and peace of mind. Paired seamlessly with my home assistant via Zigbee2MQTT, this little device has become an indispensable guardian against potential water disasters.

    Installation was a breeze, thanks to its compact design and straightforward setup instructions. Within minutes, it was operational and ready to safeguard against leaks under the sink or even around my hot tub area. The sensor's sensitivity is impressive, promptly detecting even the slightest hint of moisture and sending an instant alert to my smartphone.

    The integration with Zigbee2MQTT ensures that I can monitor the sensor's status and receive notifications directly through my preferred home automation platform. This level of connectivity allows for seamless integration into my existing smart home ecosystem, enhancing its functionality without complexity.

    What truly sets the Aqara Water Leak Sensor apart is its reliability. During testing, it responded swiftly to simulated leaks, triggering alerts without fail. This responsiveness gives me confidence that my home is protected around the clock, whether I'm nearby or miles away.

    In conclusion, if you're looking to fortify your home against water-related mishaps with a dependable and easy-to-use solution, look no further than the Aqara Water Leak Sensor. It's a must-have for any smart home enthusiast seeking both functionality and peace of mind.

    The information suggests pairing with an aqara hub, but as they're zigbee devices, they also pair with my sonoff zigbee dongle plus. Using ZHA they expose moisture (wet or dry), device temp (as expected, this runs hotter than ambient temperature) , firmware and battery. The battery showed 84% immediately, then rapidly 73% - this is something I've noticed with some of my other aqara zigbee devices, although the battery then seems to stay very stable at that level for a long time.

    The first time I tried to pair the device was unsuccessful. A 5 second press of the reset button didn't seem to make if visible to my zigbee network. The second time, I bought it close to my zigbee dongle, and held the reset button until the blue light flashed, and continued to hold the button until it paired with ZHA - this took approximately 20 seconds.

    In a crude test I poured about 10 ml of water next to the device and let it trickly underneath - it took about a minute, but then triggered my leak detection automation. I think it took some time for the water to spread and get in contact with the 2 sensors which are underneath the device. When I remove it from the water, it immediately records dry. When I placed it back in the small 10ml pool of water on the surface, it immediately recorded wet again.

    I'm pretty happy that this will rapidly detect a fairly small leak.

    I have been using the Aqara Water Leak Sensor for a few months now and I have to say, I am extremely impressed with its performance. This sensor is designed to detect water leaks and alert you immediately, which can help prevent costly water damage.

    The installation process was very easy, it comes with a double-sided adhesive tape which I used to stick it to the floor near any potential water leaks, such as under the sink, near the washing machine, etc. It also comes with a CR2450 battery that lasts for about two years.

    One of the things I appreciate the most about this sensor is its sensitivity, it can detect even the smallest amount of water and sends an alert to my smartphone through the Aqara app. I have set it up to send notifications to my phone and it has worked flawlessly, I have received alerts even when the water leak was very small.

    I also like that it is compatible with other smart home devices, such as my smart plugs, and I can set up automations to turn off the water supply when it detects a leak. This feature gives me peace of mind knowing that even if I am not home, my smart devices will act on it.

    Overall, I think the Aqara Water Leak Sensor is an excellent investment for anyone looking to prevent water damage in their home. It is easy to install, extremely sensitive, and can be integrated with other smart home devices. I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a reliable water leak sensor.

  • michele
    5 out of 5 stars
    Ottimo sensore rilevazione perdita acqua
    Reviewed in Italy on 6 July 2025
    Pattern Name: Single
    Verified Purchase
    Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
    Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

    Il sensore di perdite d'acqua Aqara SJCGQ11LM è un dispositivo Zigbee progettato per rilevare la presenza di acqua in ambienti domestici o professionali e segnalare tempestivamente eventuali perdite, allagamenti o infiltrazioni. È compatibile con l'ecosistema Aqara Home, Apple HomeKit, Home Assistant (tramite Zigbee2MQTT o ZHA) e altre piattaforme compatibili con Zigbee.

    Caratteristiche principali:

    - Protocollo di comunicazione: Zigbee (Zigbee 1.2)

    - Alimentazione: CR2032 (sostituibile)

    - Classe di protezione: IP67 (resistente a polvere e immersione temporanea)

    - Rilevamento tramite due pin metallici alla base

    - Design compatto

    Pregi:

    1. Affidabilità impeccabile nel tempo

    Dopo oltre un anno di utilizzo continuo, il sensore si è dimostrato estremamente affidabile: Zero falsi allarmi, Nessuna perdita di comunicazione Zigbee, Batteria ancora in buono stato

    Questo è uno degli aspetti più importanti per un sensore di sicurezza: non solo deve funzionare, ma deve farlo sempre. Questo Aqara lo fa egregiamente.

    2. Installazione facilissima

    Non richiede alcuna configurazione complicata. Basta accoppiarlo al coordinatore Zigbee tramite premendo sul simbolo "goccia", posizionarlo nel punto desiderato (es. sotto lavandini, vicino alla lavatrice o alla caldaia) e dimenticarsene. Funziona da subito.

    3. Compattezza e discrezione

    Il design minimale e le dimensioni ridotte permettono di posizionarlo ovunque senza intralcio. Non ha cavi, è leggerissimo e può essere messo anche sotto mobili bassi.

    4. Compatibilità eccellente

    Funziona perfettamente con Home Assistant, sia con ZHA che con Zigbee2MQTT, e di conseguenza può essere integrato in automazioni avanzate, come: Notifiche istantanee, attivazione sirene, chiusura automatica dell'elettrovalvola dell'acqua

    5. Impermeabilità certificata IP67

    Può essere tranquillamente esposto ad acqua e umidità. In caso di allagamento, continua a comunicare senza problemi.

    Difetti

    1. Nessun test manuale integrato

    Non c’è un pulsante di “test allarme”. Per testarlo, bisogna fisicamente bagnare i due elettrodi. Una funzione di test sarebbe comoda per verificare periodicamente il corretto funzionamento.

    2. Manca un allarme acustico integrato

    Il dispositivo non emette alcun suono: in caso di allarme, serve un sistema domotico per notificare l’utente o attivare un avvisatore esterno. Se viene usato in modo standalone, non segnala nulla da solo.

    3. Comunicazione unidirezionale e senza feedback

    Il sensore non invia aggiornamenti regolari se non rileva cambiamenti (non invia heartbeat frequenti come altri sensori). Anche se ciò contribuisce a prolungare la durata della batteria, può creare incertezza sul suo stato di salute se non monitorato correttamente.

    4. Versione Zigbee 1.2

    Pur funzionando benissimo, il supporto al protocollo Zigbee 3.0 (presente nei modelli più recenti Aqara) garantisce interoperabilità e aggiornamenti futuri migliori. Questo modello resta comunque molto valido, ma è tecnicamente meno moderno.

    Batteria: Dopo oltre 12 mesi di utilizzo la batteria non è ancora da sostituire, anzi segna 70%

    Questo conferma la bassissima richiesta energetica del dispositivo.

    Conclusioni

    Il sensore di perdite d'acqua Aqara SJCGQ11LM è una scelta eccellente per chi cerca un dispositivo semplice, affidabile e integrabile in un sistema domotico. Dopo oltre un anno di utilizzo, si è dimostrato totalmente privo di problemi: mai una disconnessione, mai un falso positivo, mai un segnale mancato.

    Consigliato soprattutto se hai un ecosistema Zigbee già funzionante. È il tipo di sensore “installalo e dimenticalo” che dà sicurezza reale, senza bisogno di manutenzione frequente.

    Pro:

    Funzionamento impeccabile nel tempo

    Facilità di installazione

    Design compatto e impermeabile

    Ottima integrazione in domotica

    Contro:

    Nessun allarme sonoro integrato

    Protocollo Zigbee 1.2

    Manca un test di autodiagnostica

    Si, lo consiglierei ad occhi chiusi ad amici e parenti

    Update - 11-29-2023:

    Added temperature sensor info below and attached image.

    Original Review:

    Bought these since they were on sale and wanted something to integrate to Home Assistant. Wasn't super on board with the idea of a "coin" style water detector (would prefer the cable type), but went with this to give it a shot. I put it next to the drain and water heater downstairs.

    Fast forward three months. We had a small backup in our drain downstairs and the alarm in Home Assistant went off. Saved me a lot of damage I'm sure. You will 100% want to make sure you set up multiple critical notifications in your automation and consider choosing a custom obnoxious sound. If you're sleeping, you want to make sure you don't sleep through it.

    The Good:

    -- Paid for itself already

    -- Integrated very nicely with my Sonoff receiver in Home Assistant.

    -- Fairly non-descript and small. Hard to notice on the floor.

    -- Fast. This thing went off immediately when water had reached it.

    -- Inexpensive! I'll be honest, I really wish there was a cable type Zigbee detector that wasn't $100. But this thing is just so darn inexpensive that you can get six of these for the cost of one of those plus an extension cable.

    The Cromulent:

    -- It's battery-powered. As mentioned above, I the cable type is preferred, but I'm guessing there's zero chance of a cable type without having to be plugged into an outlet. Plus you can put these wherever you need without having to worry about an outlet.

    -- TBD on battery life so far. I've been tracking this since I installed it in mid-July. Started at 88% with the factory-supplied battery (constant problem with Aqara) and within ten days it had dropped to 70%. It has been sitting there at 70% for three months now. I'll update this when I have to change batteries.

    -- The LQI shows a fairly weak connection, which is surprising given that it's only 10-15 feet away through two interior walls. Kind of surprising given that other devices that are much further away are significantly better.

    The Bad:

    -- The temperature sensors in these are utter garbage. They're the internal temperature of the device, not the room they're in. They're off by 10+ degF and should NOT be relied upon in any capacity.

    Overall:

    There really are no major primary weaknesses to this device. I'll be grabbing a couple more when they go on sale to scatter around the house. I'd like to get the Eve Water Guard but at $100 + $20/6 ft, it's really hard to justify it.

    The temperature sensors are useless cost adders and Aqara would be better off just removing them.

About this Item

  • NOTES: Aqara Hub is required and sold separately. Requires a secured 2. 4 gigahertz WiFi network connection. One Aqara Hub can connect up to 32 Aqara devices.
  • FLOOD DETECTION: Whenever the Aqara Water Leak Sensor detects water, it can send an alert to your phone and activate the local alarm on the Aqara Hub to prevent leaks and flooding.
  • HOME AUTOMATION: Controls and triggers Aqara connected devices when excess water is detected.
  • WIRELESS & SENSITIVE: No wiring or screws are required. The ultra mini design allows you to put it anywhere that dripping and leaking could happen. Our water leak sensor is designed with sensitive leak probes which the threshold of the water level is 0.5mm.
  • INDUSTRY-LEADING QUALITY: Durable IP67 water-proof housing with rust-proof exterior coating. Zigbee2MQTT and comparable third-party USB dongles are not officially supported by Aqara. Full product functionality may be limited or unavailable.
